_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: You ruled all nine calls on the subject–discipline sheet and they are built. Five subject codes went into the map, which filled seven of the courses that had no discipline; HOSP stayed out because its own courses split four ways. Five subjects where the map disagreed with its courses now read the way the courses do — ATHL is Kinesiology, THTR is Drama/Theater Arts, and so on — which took the disagreements from nine to four. Your note on ATHL was the most useful thing on the sheet: it sent me to check whether anything would quietly merge ATHL into KINE, and the answer is that a re-mint step would have, except that someone caught it in June and blocked it. That block was one line of code and nothing else knew about it; it is now written into the canonical-subject file, so every screen that reads that file knows ATHL is deliberately its own code. One correction to my own sheet: I called ESLN's discipline name malformed, and it is not — that name, and seven others, come to us that way from the official Minimum Qualifications index, which prints a Title 5 section number beside the title. Repairing it is a bigger job than the sheet said and is queued on its own.

items.text: Four subjects are left where the map and the courses disagree, down from nine after your ruling. ETHN is the substantial one: the map says Ethnic Studies and 34 courses sit under Chicano Studies. PHTO is thin — the map says Photography and only 3 of its 12 courses say Multimedia, so the row overstates it. ENVS is a single course. ESLN is the name problem below, not a real disagreement. All four now say so on the row, which they did not before.

The live-session banner is on and pointing at today's session. Open COBI and check it reads the way you want. Two things to know: only people on the Team & RACI roster, or anyone who has entered the team phrase, can see it — college users and the public cannot. And whoever opens the link sees where the session had got to when they clicked; they reload for anything newer. That is why it says reload rather than watch.

The Sky draws almost twice as fast as it did this morning. Open SkyView and say whether the drift reads smoothly now. If it still steps, the next lever is drawing fewer points per frame, which is what worked the last three times.

The accessibility sweep across COBI went from all 38 tabs failing to 19. One line did most of it: the checkbox labeled “Don’t greet me with paintings” was 20 pixels tall where the standard asks for 24, and it sits on every tab, so it failed every tab on its own. The remaining 19 tabs are counted and named — 71 separate color and target-size problems — and are engineering work rather than anything you need to rule on. Nothing here changes what any tab shows you.

The CPL face and the light are on the map — open SkyView, press CPL and Articulations, or use the link #skyview/cpl. Two questions only you can answer: does the credential-led label read right at your zoom, and is Articulations the word you want on the button? Everything else on the face follows your eight rulings as written.

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification is the natural pilot.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. DR-24 now carries your name as its owner; say the word and the phrase gets scoped.

The 19 COBI tabs still failing the accessibility sweep: 71 distinct failing selectors, 5,332 sub-24px targets and 22 scrolling regions no keyboard can reach. our-process is six faults from two color tokens and pipeline is ten, so the first few tabs are cheap. This is the shape that pays for fanning out — many surfaces, and every hit verified by re-running one command.

86 course identities still have no discipline, down from 93. They are a named curator list now, not a silent residue: kb/discipline_blanks_worklist.json gives every subject code, its waiting courses and — the column that matters — what could be used to check a proposed answer. For 37 of the 45 codes the answer is nothing at all. The daily run rebuilds it.

Eight discipline names in our Minimum Qualifications list carry a Title 5 section number that belongs beside the title, not in it — 53412 for noncredit basic skills and ESL, 53414 for the DSPS disciplines. It shows in only 45 live courses, but the strings appear 1,183 times across 33 files including the minted-course record and four alias maps, so this is an identifier rename with a dry run and a receipt, not a find-and-replace. Its own PR.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

Two housekeeping items behind the CPL face. Fifty-five exhibits in the articulation crosswalk are no longer in today's MAP feed; they stay on the map flagged in words rather than dropped, and the fix is a re-seed of the crosswalk from a fresh custom report. And the credit-funnel numbers the face carries for context were read by hand on 2026-09-07; refresh them after the next custom-report load.

Decision packs still only exist for 5 of the 159 disciplines because they are baked into the page. Fetching them per discipline the way the course descriptions already are is the bottleneck behind several of the remaining asks.
